entry.title: CrossCode v0.9.5
entry.content:
## Changes to Logic
* Modified **Faj'ro Temple** and **Grand Krys'kajo** logic (#90, @Valkhiya). * Both temples now have their initial doors leading to the middle of the temple unlocked by default. * Now, completing the left and right branches of the first floor of each temple, instead of unlocking the next part of the dungeon, spawns a chest. * This relaxes the number of required elements needed to finish these temples, leading to more possible logical permutations. * **Note:** These patches are not applied conditionally. If you generated on 0.9.4 or before and you want to avoid going out of logic, you will have to enforce this on your own by only accessing the second floor of the dungeons only after completing both branches. * Removed Chest Lock Randomization from **Mine U2: Frozen Chamber 2 Right**, **Faj'ro 3F: Large Fire Chamber Right**, and **So'najiz U1: Trial of Persistence Lower Left** (#91, @CodeTriangle). * These chests are the game's introduction to the concept of using **Thief's Key**, **Silver Key**, and **Radiant Key** respectively, meaning that they control barriers to progression. * When **Chest Lock Randomization** was enabled, however, these chests would generate with a random level, causing a long-standing logic bug. * Now, these chests will always generate with their default level, ensuring logical accuracy.
## Fixes to Generation
* Do not create regions that will not be used in the rando (CodeTriangle/Archipelago#26, #92, @CodeTriangle). * This fixes a unit test failure.
## Fixes to Logic
* Move **Henry Trailblazing** to **Sapphire Ridge** region.

entry.title: Metroid Dread v0.26.0
entry.content:
## ⚠️ Breaking: `lights_out` is now `disabled_lights`
The old `lights_out` toggle was a map-**hide** race mode that shipped with unconfirmed GUI object paths, so on real hardware it silently did nothing. It has been replaced by a faithful port of Randovania's per-region **disabled lights**, which deletes each chosen region's light actors from the RomFS — the Dairon-powered-down look, applied region-wide:
```yaml Metroid Dread: disabled_lights: - dairon - cataris ```
Valid regions: `artaria`, `burenia`, `cataris`, `dairon`, `elun`, `ferenia`, `ghavoran`, `hanubia`, `itorash`. It's purely visual — logic, the item pool and solvability are unaffected at any accessibility level.
**If your YAML sets `lights_out`**, remove it — it's now an unknown option (Archipelago warns and ignores it). Nothing is lost; it never did anything.
## Also in this release
- **Fixed: couldn't stay connected with Speed Booster Conservation disabled** ([#172](https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/issues/172)). A seed with dropped locations sent the server a location id the slot doesn't hold, which raised a server-side error and dropped the client — an endless connect → scout → kick → reconnect loop every 10 s. The client now only scouts and hints locations the slot actually holds.
## What's Changed
* chore(release): v0.25.0 by @mdietz94 in https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/pull/170 * Only scout/hint locations the slot actually holds (fixes #172) by @mdietz94 in https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/pull/173 * feat(options)!: replace "Lights Out" map-hide with RDV's real per-region disabled lights by @mdietz94 in https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/pull/174
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/compare/v0.25.0...v0.26.0
## Installation
1. Download `dread.apworld` (below) and drop it into your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` directory. 2. Generate a multiworld using `Metroid Dread` as the game. 3. Launch the **Dread Client** from Archipelago's Launcher (or open a `.dreadap` file). The window includes an AP server address bar, a **"Dread"** tab (live status + log), and a top-bar **Switch-status pill** for pointing the client at your Switch or Ryujinx. Click the pill → edit the IP → **Reconnect** (or use `/dread_connect <ip>` in the command bar). 4. Run `/setup` in the client to build and deploy the patched RomFS — see the [first-time setup walkthrough](https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/blob/main/docs/first-time-setup.md) for the click-by-click guide.
See [README.md](https://github.com/mdietz94/dread_ap/blob/main/README.md) for prerequisites (Switch hardware, Atmosphere CFW, Dread 2.1.0 RomFS, etc.).

entry.title: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster v1.1.0
entry.content:
## Logic
The bulk of this release. Logic was reworked to model the mall the way the game actually plays.
- Entrance Plaza: shutters now gate everything behind them, including the four display racks and the Backup for Brad interaction; EP routing restricted to real paths - Maintenance Tunnel modelled in both modes, and the door graph completed in both directions - Microwave and stove checks now sum across reachable zones instead of assuming a single area; Seon's stays required in Restricted Item Mode, and received food items can stand in for it otherwise - Region-level logic for level-up checks - Revised gating for A Promise to Isabela, Out of Control, and Beat Drivin Carlito in ScoopSanity - Backup for Brad can no longer land in the first ScoopSanity chain slot - Ammo logic revised for the 30/300 bullet checks - Challenge checks can be satisfied by sent tools outside Restricted Item Mode - Universal Tracker now adopts the seed's own scoop order when re-generating
## Options and items
- New **Cult Limited** toggle
## Client and stability
- Fixed the first Connect never completing — no more pressing Connect twice - Slot-connect and item delivery deferred a frame, fixing unreliable reads during load - Bundled REFramework updated to v1.5.9.1, which fixes the garbled console output and the memory corruption behind it - Every play session writes its own timestamped log file - The mod now fails visibly if the client DLL can't load, instead of silently - Survives prefab registry loss in the world spawner - Traps fire at most one per area at a time - Traps, buffs and other unusable items no longer clutter the item list; the unused Saves tab is gone
## Packaging
- **The zip now includes `reframework/data`.** It was missing from earlier releases, which left the mod loading with no item data on a clean install. - Shipped as a single zip with REFramework, the client library and licences
## Docs
- New Beginner's Guide - New Known Bugs document - README updated to match the current install layout
## Known issues
- **Rescue Simone Ravendark** is force-excluded this release. The rescue broke between 1.0.2 and 1.1.0; excluding it keeps the check from stranding anyone while the root cause is fixed. Tracked in #16.
## Upgrading
Extract the zip over your existing install and let it overwrite — the `reframework/data` folder is new and the mod will not work without it.
## Credits
Logic work by @Mr-Rippe and @RazgrizEast.

entry.title: Kirby & The Amazing Mirror v0.3.0
entry.content:
### New Features
- Ability gating is now available and under the `Make the game harder` option group. It defaults to be "on". A preset list of abilities is available at the beginning of the game (Beam, Burning, Mini, Stone, and Wheel). This list should be the bare minimum you need to complete the game and get all the currently supported locations. All other abilities are gated by custom AP items (for example, "Sword Ability") (Issues #855, #819). - Added a new goal mode: `defeat_configured_area_boss` completes the seed after a specific area-boss is defeated (Issue #207). - Which area boss is used is determined by the new `configured_area_boss` option. It defaults to Master Hand and Crazy Hand. - Added four new lever location checks sourced from native lever bits: Moonlight Mansion 2-11, Olive Ocean 6-13, Carrot Castle 5-12, and Radish Ruins 8-12 (Issue #850). - Added the world map big chest in the tutorial rooms as an AP location check (Issue #845). We plan for the world map as an item to follow later. - Because of how we detect the game state, the check will only send AFTER the tutorial is completed and you enter Central Circle for the first time.
### Improvements
- Self-send item popups in BizHawk are now collapsed to one line (`You found your <item>.`) instead of separate send and receive popups (Issue #848).
### Known Limitations - Localization: Only the North American ROM is supported. All AP notifications are in English. - Progression: The entire game is still only two spheres. This means you can complete almost the entirety of Kirby and the Amazing Mirror without ever having to receive an item, except open the Dimension Mirror. In other words, you can do everything in the game except defeat Dark Mind without ever receiving an item from another player. This is a consequence of the original game design. We have plans to gate your progression in other ways, but they all require coding/hacking in intentional blockers. - Small Chests: We know you want the "small" chests implemented. We want them implemented too. We've been working on it for months. We decided getting out what IS working, is more important. - Sprite Swapping: The animation for getting the original item will play with the original sprite. Statues show the old ability. This is expected. We hope in the future to support "sprite swapping" where we show the sprite for the actual item delivered or ability granted. - Emulator: Only BizHawk is supported. mGBA may work, but we don't currently test against it.
### Bug Fixes
- Prevent false LocationChecks after death by deferring polling while HP <= 0 (Issue #864). - In `completely_random` mode, enabled regular ability statues now make a fresh per-touch draw from the configured statue pool instead of repeating their generation-time fallback assignment. The draw honors custom whitelists, the Minny toggle, and live ability unlocks while preserving statue-specific exclusions for no-ability and enemy-source toggles (Issue #875). - When `ability_randomization_mode` was `completely_random` and `ability_randomization_statues` was enabled, statue abilities were just shuffled, not random (Issue #841). - Changed map and shard item grants to be only additive, never overwriting what was already in the save. This was a consequence of how I "replayed" certain item grants when a game was opened again (PR #881). - Fixed hub-switch first-poll baseline suppression so reconnect/disconnect windows do not drop legitimate big-switch location checks (Issue #879). - Apply `Starting Kirby Color` before the first gameplay palette is created and explicitly refresh the live OBJ palette after reconnects, savestates, or soft resets (Issue #852).
### Internal Changes
- Added seed-specific initial-gate and statue-pool masks, executable native-C policy tests, client compatibility tests, ROM-token tests, and patch-callsite contracts for the statue runtime path. - Fixed `patch_rom.py` importing on supported Python versions by typing the multiprocessing queue with its actual class rather than subscripting the `multiprocessing.Queue` factory. - Log files now report the `world_version` and all game options (Issue #861). - Added file-only telemetry diagnostics for ability statue grants when `ability_randomization_mode` is `shuffled` or `completely_random`, goal target resolution (one-time per session), runtime ability config rewrites (mask/seed snapshot on change), mailbox ACK timeout aggregates, and explicit statue ability-gate suppression reasons (PR #867). - Expand the allowed versions of requirements.txt (PR #881). - Reduce generated `kirbyam.apworld` size by excluding `worlds/kirbyam/save_states` and `worlds/kirbyam/kirby_ap_payload/patch_rom.log` from world packaging, and add explicit ignore entries for KirbyAM-local cache/log artifacts (Issue #871).
### Other
- Create a new AI disclosure page.

entry.title: Muse Dash v1.5.35
entry.content:
# Changes - Update songs to Song of Determination & Power - If the mod fails to get datastorage values on startup, it should continue on and give you free items (for now) rather than crash internally and put the mod in a bad state.
# Installation ## Melonloader *Melonloader is required to play with this mod. However reinstalling it is not required on update.*
> You can find Muse Dash's folder by finding the game in your steam library, right clicking it and choosing *Manage→Browse Local Files*.
### Windows 1. Download `MelonLoader.Installer.exe` from https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader/releases/latest and run it. 2. Select Muse Dash in the list of games. - If Muse Dash does not appear, click add game manually then browse to `MuseDash.exe`. 3. Click install. - If the latest version is not working: **Untick Latest and select 0.7.2**
### Linux 1. Navigate to Muse Dash on steam, open properties and add the following to Launch Options: `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="version=n,b" %command%` 2. Download `MelonLoader.Installer.Linux` from https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader/releases/latest and run it. - You may need to give it permissions to execute. 3. Select Muse Dash in the list of games. - If Muse Dash does not appear, click add game manually then browse to `MuseDash.exe`. 4. Click install. On first run, melonloader may install dotnet 6 in order to run. - If the latest version is not working: **Untick Latest and select 0.7.2**
### Mod Install 1.Download `ArchipelagoMuseDash.zip`. 2. Head to the Muse Dash folder and open up `/mods/`. If this folder does not exist, run the game and it should appear. 3. Extract the contents of the .zip file into mods. Ensure the files are not in a subfolder, this mod is not setup for that yet. 4. Run the game. If a new button appears on the start screen the mod was installed correctly.

entry.title: Once Upon a Katamari v0.3.0
entry.content:
This updated mod is compatible with worlds generated using v0.1.0 and v0.2.x. The apworld is not compatible with older versions of the mod. ## Collectionsanity Collectionsanity allows you to turn (almost) every single unique roll in the game into a check. The 'BAN', 'DAI', 'NAM' and 'CO' objects, as well as all objects unique to the final "That Hole..." level are not currently included. A total of 3,637 objects are included. You can choose between 'individual' and 'milestones' mode. Individual means every unique object is considered a check. E.g. you get a check for specifically rolling up a tomato. Milestones means you gain checks for every x amount of unique objects rolled up. If you set it to 100, you'll get a check for rolling up 100 unique objects, and then 200 and so on. You can also set an amount of objects to be considered 'out of logic', so you don't have to hunt down every single object. Unless you want to. Objects found in the tutorial are not considered in logic as they are missable. You can set a percentage of collectionsanity checks on either mode to be forced to have a local junk item. ## Other Changes - You can now skip the tutorial - "As Large As Possible 1" is no longer a forced starting level. - Start with a random cousin - Fog Trap - Adds the fog from the 'Lots of Yokai' stage as a trap, which will slowly dissipate over time (does not activate on 'Lots of Yokai') - The preview shown before starting a level will now accurately show which crowns, cousins and presents you have collected in that level.
See the [README](https://github.com/ItsSeafoamy/Once-Upon-an-Archipelago/blob/main/README.md) for more info and setup instructions.
*it was mainly collectionsanity :3*
